messages:
maya: Quick question — for the new deploy-hooks service account, do we give it Org Viewer or a project-level deploy role? It needs to trigger infra pipelines across prod projects but must not read logs/secrets. cc @samir

samir: Org Viewer is too broad. Aim for a custom project role scoped to only the permissions it needs (least-priv). What cloud provider/project boundaries are we talking about?

maya: GCP. Hooks live in a shared infra project and need to trigger Cloud Build in infra-prod and apps-prod and read build status. They should NOT be able to read logs or GCS artifacts.

leo: Suggest a custom role that includes only: cloudbuild.builds.create, cloudbuild.builds.get, cloudbuild.builds.list (if you need list), and optionally iam.serviceAccounts.actAs if it needs to impersonate a runner SA. If using pubsub for trigger delivery add pubsub.topics.publish.

julie: Also remember cross-project bindings: you'll need roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on the target service account if the hook impersonates one. For logs: do NOT add any storage.objects.get or logging.logEntries.list. We redact secrets at ingestion but avoid granting read rights where possible.

maya: Can someone paste a minimal gcloud snippet we can apply as a starting point?

samir: Sure — basic example to create a custom role and bind the SA (edit permissions as needed):

```bash
# create custom role in infra-shared project
gcloud iam roles create DeployHookRunner --project=infra-shared \
  --title="Deploy Hook Runner" \
  --permissions="cloudbuild.builds.create,cloudbuild.builds.get,cloudbuild.builds.list,pubsub.topics.publish" \
  --stage="GA"

# bind service account to the custom role in infra-shared
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding infra-shared \
  --member="serviceAccount:deploy-hooks@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="projects/infra-shared/roles/DeployHookRunner"
```

leo: Add iam.serviceAccounts.actAs if the hook needs to run steps as another SA. For cross-project triggers, bind the SA in the target project(s) too.

julie: Ops note — avoid long-lived project-level bindings. Use short TTL and record expiry in the approval. Also add a runbook entry explaining what the role is used for.

maya: Thanks. Do we need an explicit security approval for this since it touches prod infra?

samir: Yes — file a brief request in #security-approvals with justification, resources, who needs access, and an expiry. I can approve up to 48h for testing; anything longer needs a writeup and product/infra sign-off.

julie: +1. Also include a note on logs redaction and confirm no storage objects read is required.

deploy-bot: Policy change request created: PR #342 for infra-shared roles — https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/342

maya: Filed the approval request and attached the PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/342 — assigning to @samir for review and adding an expiry timestamp in the description. Thanks :thumbsup:
